articles.title: Watch: Dana White declines Trump’s offer to be White House press secretary
articles.summary: In a social media post over the weekend, the president asked the UFC boss to take over the role, but later said he was "having a little fun".
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White declined President Donald Trump's offer to be the next White House press secretary during a briefing on Monday.

The president had asked White to take over the role in a social post over the weekend. Trump later said he was "having a little fun".

During the briefing, White confirmed he won't take the job as he doesn't "want to be in politics."

articles.title: Bernie Sanders, Annie Andrews float impeaching RFK Jr.
articles.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders was asked if he agreed with South Carolina Sen.-elect Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, who wants Robert F. Kennedy impeached at HHS.
articles.body:
Sen. Bernie Sanders , who is poised to chair the Senate's health committee next year, said in a new interview that he's open to impeaching Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

The independent Vermont senator, who caucuses with Democrats, appeared on CNN's "State of the Union" with Dana Bash on Nov. 8 after a wave of Democratic wins in last week's midterms.

Bash asked Sanders if he agreed with South Carolina Sen.-elect Annie Andrews , a pediatrician, saying that Kennedy should be removed from his role as the nation's top health official.

"I am absolutely open to that," Sanders said of Andrews' view. "The bottom line is we need a secretary of HHS who is concerned about the health and well-being of our kids and all Americans, not involved in crazy conspiracy theories."

He continued, "I'm open to all ideas from Dr. Andrews or anybody else."

In a statement, HHS spokesperson Grace Jamison said "Secretary Kennedy has delivered the most sweeping public health reforms in modern history."

"He will continue to put prevention at the center of health care to end the chronic disease epidemic and Make America Healthy Again," Jamison said. "Threats of impeachment will not distract him from delivering for the American people."

Amy Acton, Annie Andrews and what Dem wins mean for RFK Jr. and the MAHA movement

As health secretary, and during his previous 2020 presidential campaign, Kennedy heralded the "Make America Healthy Again," or MAHA movement, which promised and promoted sweeping changes to America's health ecosystem including policy shifts in nutrition and medicine.

But Kennedy has long faced bipartisan criticism for skepticism over vaccines .

Andrews, who prevailed over appointed Sen. Darline Graham , will be the Senate's first pediatrician. Andrews' criticism of RFK Jr. and the Trump administration's handling of health care was a core part of her argument on the campaign trail.

Bash asked Sanders about how he planned to handle Kennedy's tenure as he's expected to take the health committee chairmanship next year, after Democrats gained seven Senate seats so far this midterm cycle and the Senate majority.

articles.title: Ministério pede derrubada de 348 perfis de influenciadores que divulgam bets ilegais | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a pasta, as contas somam mais de 150 milhões de seguidores. Medida Provisória proibiu a exploração e a publicidade das apostas no país.
articles.summary: Segundo a pasta, as contas somam mais de 150 milhões de seguidores. Medida Provisória proibiu a exploração e a publicidade das apostas no país.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública (MJSP) solicitou a derrubada de 348 perfis de influenciadores digitais usados para divulgar plataformas de apostas ilegais nas redes sociais .

Segundo a pasta, as contas, todas no Instagram, somam mais de 150 milhões de seguidores. Entre os alvos está um perfil com 1,4 milhão de seguidores. O pedido foi encaminhado às plataformas.

O ministério afirma que a medida faz parte de uma ofensiva para impedir que plataformas clandestinas utilizem influenciadores e redes sociais para alcançar novos apostadores.

➡️ O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) publicou, em 25 de setembro, a MP que proibiu a exploração, a oferta, a intermediação e a publicidade das apostas de quota fixa no país, além de jogos on-line e cassinos virtuais.

Segundo o ministério, somente nesta segunda também foram identificadas:

2.207 páginas no Facebook, que somam audiência de 7,5 milhões;

18 grupos no Telegram, com aproximadamente 182 mil participantes;

998 sites relacionados a apostas irregulares.

“Não basta retirar do ar os sites de apostas ilegais se essas plataformas continuam chegando à população por meio de influenciadores e redes sociais. Estamos atuando sobre toda essa cadeia de divulgação para impedir que atividades clandestinas continuem explorando os cidadãos e comprometendo a renda das famílias”, afirmou o ministro da Justiça, Wellington César Lima e Silva, segundo nota da pasta.

O monitoramento é feito pela Secretaria Nacional de Direitos Digitais (Sedigi) e pela Secretaria Nacional de Segurança Pública (Senasp), por meio do Laboratório de Operações Cibernéticas (Ciberlab). O trabalho envolve sites, redes sociais e aplicativos de mensagens.

De acordo com o Ministério da Justiça, o monitoramento iniciado em 25 de setembro já contabilizou mais de 60 mil sites, páginas, perfis, grupos e servidores relacionados à divulgação de apostas irregulares.

A pasta afirma ainda ter identificado 6.596 páginas no Facebook, que somam audiência de 34 milhões de membros e seguidores, além de mais de 900 perfis no Instagram.

No Telegram, foram identificados 1.442 grupos, que reúnem 25,6 milhões de participantes. O levantamento também encontrou 127 perfis no TikTok, com 469 mil seguidores.

Segundo o ministério, em 9 de outubro o levantamento contabilizava 20.318 sites, páginas, perfis, grupos e servidores. Um mês depois, o número ultrapassou 60 mil.

A ofensiva ocorre após o governo federal proibir as apostas de quota fixa no país, as chamadas bets. A proibição foi estabelecida pela Medida Provisória nº 1.394, publicada em 25 de setembro.

A medida provisória proibiu a exploração, a oferta, a intermediação e a publicidade das apostas de quota fixa no Brasil. A medida também alcançou jogos on-line e cassinos virtuais, como o chamado “Jogo do Tigrinho”.

A retirada de conteúdos relacionados às apostas nas redes sociais já estava entre as frentes de atuação do governo.

Em 29 de setembro, o Ministério da Justiça informou ter solicitado o bloqueio de 5.209 sites e a remoção de 186 aplicativos das lojas da Apple e do Google. Na ocasião, também haviam sido solicitadas as remoções de 300 páginas no Facebook e 90 perfis no Instagram.

O governo também notificou Google, Meta, YouTube, X, Telegram, TikTok, Kwai e Discord para retirar propagandas irregulares.

Mesmo após a proibição, influenciadores continuaram divulgando plataformas de apostas. Em outubro, o g1 identificou ao menos 40 perfis de influenciadores no Ceará que ainda publicavam links de bets e cassinos virtuais no Instagram .

A MP estabeleceu ainda um“dever de cuidado” para plataformas digitais, que devem adotar medidas para impedir a circulação de conteúdos relacionados aos serviços proibidos.

As empresas também devem retirar publicações e anúncios considerados irregulares quando notificadas pelas autoridades competentes.

Em paralelo à medida provisória, o governo enviou ao Congresso um projeto de lei que prevê criminalizar a exploração e a divulgação de apostas .

Pelo texto encaminhado aos parlamentares, fazer propaganda ou marketing para incentivar apostas, recrutar apostadores ou monetizar esse tipo de publicidade poderá ser punido com dois a quatro anos de prisão e multa, caso a proposta seja aprovada.

Segundo o Ministério da Justiça, o monitoramento de sites, redes sociais e aplicativos de mensagens continuará para identificar novos canais utilizados na divulgação de plataformas ilegais. A pasta afirma que denúncias podem ser encaminhadas pelo Fala.BR.

articles.title: Presidente do Supremo arquiva definitivamente o inquérito das fake news | G1
articles.standfirst: O ministro Edson Fachin atendeu ao parecer favorável da Procuradoria-Geral da República.
articles.summary: O ministro Edson Fachin atendeu ao parecer favorável da Procuradoria-Geral da República.
articles.body:
O presidente do STF - Supremo Tribunal Federal , ministro Edson Fachin , decidiu na noite desta segunda-feira (9) arquivar o inquérito das fake news, aberto há mais de sete anos para apurar ataques ao STF e a seus integrantes. Ao longo do tempo, a investigação foi alvo de críticas pela ampliação da finalidade e sucessivas prorrogações. O repórter Vladimir Netto, tem todos os detalhes:

"Esse inquérito das fake news foi aberto há sete anos, em 2019. Na época, o então presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal, ministro Dias Toffoli, escolheu o ministro Alexandre de Moraes para ser o relator do caso. E hoje, a Procuradoria-Geral da República enviou um parecer ao presidente do Supremo, Edson Fachin, defendendo o fim dessa investigação, o arquivamento dela. Agora à noite, o presidente do Supremo concordou com esse pedido da PGR e determinou o arquivamento do inquérito. Fachin disse que 'já não se encontra fundamento bastante para a manutenção indefinida do procedimento, sem reavaliação concreta da necessidade de sua continuidade como investigação matriz'. Sobre o sigilo das investigações, Fachin disse que devem ser 'resguardados dados relacionados à intimidade e vida privada de pessoas e autoridades públicas mencionadas ao longo das apurações'. O presidente do Supremo também argumentou que 'a proteção das instituições democráticas, não menos que a persecução daqueles que atentem contra elas, há de realizar-se dentro da Constituição. É essa mesma Constituição que protege a independência do Poder Judiciário e que assegura a todos a razoável duração do processo, a liberdade e o devido processo legal'. Fachin também disse que o encerramento das apurações deve ser imediato, determinando o fim de toda e qualquer nova diligência".

Portanto, então, o presidente do Supremo acatou o parecer da Procuradoria-Geral da República que defendeu o arquivamento do inquérito.

O procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet , considerou que o inquérito das fake news cumpriu sua finalidade e deveria ser arquivado. O inquérito foi aberto de ofício, ou seja, sem nenhuma solicitação externa, em março de 2019, pelo então presidente do Supremo, Dias Toffoli, para apurar ataques ao STF e a seus integrantes. Toffoli escolheu o ministro Alexandre de Moraes para conduzir as investigações.

Presidente do Supremo arquiva definitivamente o inquérito das fake news — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Nesta segunda-feira (9), Gonet defendeu a investigação. Disse que " ameaças dirigidas aos ministros e a seus familiares, campanhas de desinformação financiadas e difundidas em massa e incitações ao fechamento do Tribunal voltavam-se contra a liberdade de decidir e a autoridade das decisões ".

Ao longo dos anos, decisões como bloqueios de contas nas redes sociais e buscas e apreensões provocaram críticas e divergências entre juristas, entidades e ministros. Também foram alvo de críticas a ampliação da finalidade do inquérito e as sucessivas prorrogações das investigações.

Em setembro de 2026, Fachin assumiu a condução do inquérito que era relatado por Alexandre de Moraes. O presidente do Supremo também assumiu os processos sobre os desvios do INSS e as fraudes do Banco Master, que estavam sob a relatoria do ministro André Mendonça . As decisões vieram depois de uma troca de acusações entre ministros do Supremo sobre suposto envolvimento no escândalo do Banco Master.

No fim de outubro, Fachin devolveu a Mendonça o inquérito sobre os desvios no INSS, mas manteve o caso Master sob a responsabilidade da presidência do Supremo. Ele já tinha determinado o arquivamento de nove investigações relacionadas ao inquérito das fake news.

articles.title: Em imóvel de Santiago Peña, promotores encontram passagem secreta que leva a bunker | G1
articles.standfirst: Peña foi preso logo depois de sofrer um processo de impeachment no Senado do Paraguai. Ele é suspeito de envolvimento na maior fraude financeira do país, que levou ao fechamento do Ueno Bank.
articles.summary: Peña foi preso logo depois de sofrer um processo de impeachment no Senado do Paraguai. Ele é suspeito de envolvimento na maior fraude financeira do país, que levou ao fechamento do Ueno Bank.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público do Paraguai voltou a fazer buscas em endereços do presidente deposto do país, Santiago Peña. Em um dos imóveis, os promotores encontraram uma passagem secreta que leva a um bunker. Peña é investigado por suspeita de envolvimento em fraudes no Ueno Bank, que encerrou as atividades na semana passada.

A casa de veraneio do ex-presidente Santiago Peña fica em San Bernardino, a cerca de uma hora e dez minutos de carro de Assunção. Em uma busca no domingo (8), o Ministério Público encontrou uma porta escondida em uma das paredes da casa. A passagem secreta dá acesso a um corredor que leva a um bunker.

A promotoria ainda não conseguiu entrar nessa sala, que é protegida por um sistema reforçado de segurança. Os investigadores estudam alternativas para abrir a porta. Entre as opções estão uma detonação controlada e a ajuda de algum parente do ex-presidente. Até que a porta seja aberta, a casa vai continuar lacrada e sob vigilância.

Santiago Peña foi preso na quinta-feira (5), logo depois de sofrer um processo de impeachment no Senado do Paraguai. Ele está detido em uma base militar em Assunção. Peña é suspeito de envolvimento na maior fraude financeira do país, que levou ao fechamento do Ueno Bank. O banco tinha cerca de 2,9 milhões de clientes, o equivalente a quase metade da população do Paraguai.

Em imóvel de Santiago Peña, promotores encontram passagem secreta que leva a bunker — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Na terça-feira (3), o Banco Central do Paraguai determinou o encerramento das operações do Ueno Bank, depois de constatar que o banco tinha menos da metade das garantias exigidas por lei. Santiago Peña foi sócio do grupo controlador do Ueno Bank. O encerramento das atividades do banco levou milhares de pessoas às ruas.

O então vice-presidente, Pedro Alliana, assumiu o comando do país. Nesta segunda-feira (9), ele pediu que todos os ministros e integrantes do alto escalão coloquem os cargos à disposição. Alliana disse que todas as instituições do país vão continuar funcionando normalmente.

O Banco Central do Paraguai informou que já devolveu os depósitos de cerca de 90% dos clientes do Ueno Bank e que deve concluir os pagamentos até quarta-feira (11). Mas em Cidade do Leste, a segunda mais populosa do país, tem correntistas que ainda estão com o dinheiro retido. É o caso do Mário. Ele diz que precisa do dinheiro porque tem família para alimentar, aluguel e moto para pagar.

A pesquisadora Carolina Olmedo Mendez já recebeu o dinheior que tinha no Ueno Bank, mas conta que ficou angustiada:

"Era praticamente no início do mês e eu não tinha recebido o meu salário. Então, era o dinheiro que eu contava para esperar o salário entrar. Não demorou muito para eles fazerm o estorno - que chama, né? Mas as palavras eram essas: incerteza e angústia".

articles.title: PF detalha, em relatórios, relação de Toffoli, Moraes e Nunes Marques com Vorcaro   | G1
articles.standfirst: Os relatórios foram solicitados à PF pelo presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, mas ainda não foram entregues a ele. Os delegados que elaboraram os documentos foram afastados de suas funções.
articles.summary: Os relatórios foram solicitados à PF pelo presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, mas ainda não foram entregues a ele. Os delegados que elaboraram os documentos foram afastados de suas funções.
articles.body:
Ministros do Supremo Tribunal federal (STF) Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes e Kassio Nunes Marques — Foto: STF

Investigadores da Polícia Federal (PF) concluíram na última terça-feira (3) relatórios sobre o envolvimento de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro. São três documentos, com citações aos ministros Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes e Kassio Nunes Marques.

A informação foi inicialmente publicada pela jornalista Malu Gaspar, de O Globo, e depois confirmada pela TV Globo.

Os documentos reúnem fatos com indícios de crime, alguns deles ainda não divulgados publicamente, mas não atribuem responsabilidade a ninguém. Uma eventual investigação contra um ministro da Corte dependerá do aval do plenário.

No dia seguinte à conclusão dos relatórios, na quarta-feira (4), os delegados responsáveis pelo caso Master na PF foram afastados de suas funções na coordenadoria-geral de repressão à corrupção, crimes financeiros e lavagem de dinheiro: Daniel Cola e Wedson Cajé.

Segundo fontes, eles elaboraram os relatórios.

Procurada pela reportagem, a PF negou que os relatórios estejam prontos. A direção-geral da instituição afirmou ainda que os relatórios ainda estão sendo elaborados e que serão entregues ao STF até o fim deste mês.

Em nota, a PF também afirmou que não se manifesta sobre atos de gestão de pessoal e que as dispensas de funções de confiança da corporação são atos de gestão pautados por critérios de conveniência e oportunidade administrativa.

A PF disse ainda que as funções de chefia de coordenação não implicam em qualquer alteração das equipes responsáveis pelos inquéritos em andamento na diretoria de combate ao crime organizado e à corrupção, inclusive os relacionados às operações Compliance e Sem Desconto.

Toffoli integra o quadro de sócios da Maridt Participações, empresa familiar dirigida pelos irmãos do magistrado e que fez negócios com um fundo gerido pela empresa Reag, ligada ao Banco Master .

O plenário do STF chegou a se reunir em 15 de outubro, em sessão extraordinária, para julgar o relatório que apontou vínculo entre Moraes e Vorcaro.

O julgamento, no entanto, foi suspenso após apresentação de questão de ordem pelos ministros GIlmar Mendes e Flávio Dino , sem que o mérito do caso, ou seja, a abertura ou não de investigação sobre Moraes fosse analisado.

Em relação a Kassio Nunes Marques, a PF encontrou no celular de Vorcaro um contrato de prestação de serviços entre o Banco Master e um escritório de advocacia.

Se o escritório obtivesse êxito em todas as ações judiciais, que totalizavam R$ 8,5 bilhões, os honorários advocatícios pagos poderiam chegar a R$ 427 milhões.

Mensagens trocadas por Vorcaro com Luiz Rennó, ex-diretor jurídico do Master, mencionam ainda supostos pagamentos de R$ 500 mil por mês ao advogado Kevin Marques, filho do ministro Nunes Marques.

O nome do ministro também surgiu em troca de mensagens sobre a organização de uma festa por Vorcaro para Nunes Marques com garotas de programa .

articles.title: Florida governor-elect Byron Donalds seen hanging out with Fever star Sophie Cunningham at NASCAR race
articles.summary: Byron Donalds posed with Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham at a NASCAR race, telling her to "keep speaking up" about trans athletes in sports.
articles.body:
Now that the dust has settled with the midterm elections in the rearview, it's safe to say Republicans took it on the chin.

Democrats made massive gains in both the House and Senate, and the GOP was left licking its wounds heading into a crucial 2028 election cycle.

Not all seems lost for conservatives though, particularly in the great state of Florida, where Ron DeSantis' successor Byron Donalds warded off David Jolly to keep the governor's office in Tallahassee red for at least the next four years.

Donalds ran a hell of a campaign, and after doing his part to keep my home state red, I'd say Florida's newest governor has deserved to take a bit of a victory lap, with "lap" being the operative word.

The governor-elect was out and about at the Homestead-Miami Speedway in South Florida for Sunday's big NASCAR race, taking part in some much-needed rest and relaxation following a stressful campaign.

While taking in the sights and sounds on race day, Donalds and his family ran into a familiar face and decided to pose for a photo op.

That's a lot of star power in one Instagram post.

The Indiana Fever star has drummed up plenty of controversy in recent months, going against the grain of her fellow WNBA colleagues with her seemingly conservative stances on things like trans men in women's sports.

The photo op can't just be a coincidence of two "important people" posing together for the 'Gram, and Donalds' caption seems to confirm a lot of the suspicions that Cunningham isn't just another left wing mouthpiece like some of the other players in her league.

"Keep speaking up, Sophie. The truth ALWAYS wins in the end," Donalds said, likely referring to Cunningham's comments on trans athletes.

Cunningham was recently criticized for sharing Andy Frisella's message emphasizing self-improvement over faith in elections on Instagram following the midterms.

This certainly won't help her standing with the libs, but I would venture a guess Sophie doesn't give much of a damn.

articles.title: Soto defends redistricted Florida House seat from GOP
articles.summary: Democratic Rep. Darren Soto (Fl.) is projected to survive a tough midterm challenge on Tuesday, defeating Republican Dan Green, a military veteran, to secure his sixth term on Capitol Hill, according to Decision Desk HQ. Soto’s victory was a surprise. After Florida Republicans redrew their House maps this year in favor of the GOP —…
articles.body:
Democratic Rep. Darren Soto (Fl.) is projected to survive a tough midterm challenge on Tuesday, defeating Republican Dan Green, a military veteran, to secure his sixth term on Capitol Hill, according to Decision Desk HQ.

Soto’s victory was a surprise. After Florida Republicans redrew their House maps this year in favor of the GOP — part of a larger, mid-decade redistricting campaign promoted by President Trump — the state’s 9th District shifted dramatically, eroding the power of Hispanic voters who had helped make it a relatively safe Democratic seat.

The Democrat is projected to notch about 50.3 percent of the vote while Green garnered about 49.9 percent, per DDHQ.

The changes turned a district that sided with former Vice President Kamala Harris by almost 4 percentage points in 2024 to one that favored Trump by almost 18 points. Heading into the polls, the nation’s top election handicappers had the race rated as “likely Republican.”

But this was no normal midterm cycle, and Democrats up and down the ballot were benefited by the volatility of the economy, the high cost of consumer goods throughout Trump’s second term, the blowback against the Iran war and the sheer unpopularity of the president, whose approval ratings have barely topped 30 percent in recent weeks.

Those factors helped Soto notch a stunning upset over Green, who served in the Pentagon in Trump’s first term and couldn’t escape the undertow of the president’s unpopularity.

Soto, of Puerto Rican descent, is a senior member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC), a powerful bloc of Democrats that’s led the battle against Trump’s aggressive deportation agenda.

His victory puts him in a good position to chair the CHC in the next Congress.

articles.body:
Ryan Elijah (R) is projected to defeat Bale Dalton (D) in Florida’s 7th District, according to Decision Desk HQ.

Elijah, a former news anchor who worked for WOFL-TV in Orlando for 13 years, will succeed Rep. Cory Mills (R-Fla.), whom he beat in the August GOP primary. Elijah is projected to clinch 49.7 percent of the vote while Dalton notched 49.2 percent, per DDHQ.

The House Ethics Committee has been investigating Mills since November 2025, looking into allegations of dating violence and violations of campaign finance law. Mills has denied the allegations.

Elijah defeated Mills by 13 percentage points in the primary, after which President Trump said he told the incumbent representative to drop out of the race.

The longtime journalist then knocked off Dalton, a captain in the Navy Reserve who served as chief of staff at NASA under former Administrator Bill Nelson.

Elijah campaigned on boosting America’s energy independence, curtailing government spending and protecting beaches in his district, which sits on the Atlantic coast in central Florida.

Trump also endorsed him after the primary, saying the former host of “Good Day Orlando” and “Orlando Matters” stood for “EVERYTHING MAGA.”

Elijah’s victory means a Republican will represent the 7th District for the third consecutive term. State GOP lawmakers left the district unchanged in the new congressional map they passed earlier this year.

articles.title: Biden says Trump should carry weight of US Capitol riot 'to his grave' in new book
articles.summary: Biden sharply criticises Trump in his soon-to-be released memoir, while the White House calls Biden the worst US president.
articles.body:
Former US President Joe Biden has unleashed a barrage of criticism on President Donald Trump in a soon-to-be released memoir, saying he believes the Capitol riot on 6 January 2021 "should follow him to his grave".

In an excerpt published in The Atlantic on Monday, Biden also said Trump should not have pardoned supporters who stormed Congress in a bid to thwart the certification of Biden's election victory.

"The criminals who attacked law-enforcement officers that day didn't deserve pardons," the former president wrote. "They deserved prison terms."

White House spokesperson Lauren Bis called Biden "the worst president in American history" in response to the BBC's request for comment.

In the excerpt of the book, which is due to be released later this month, Biden assailed Trump and his administration for pushing to "tear down institutions and inflame hatreds".

Biden accused him of turning a "blind eye" to their violent acts, writing: "You don't get to turn a blind eye to cops being punched, speared, sprayed, and brutalised and call yourself a friend of law enforcement."

"What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave," he said.

Trump has previously denied any wrongdoing in connection with the riot, which happened after he held a rally.

Upon returning to the White House last year, he pardoned more than 1,000 people convicted for their role in them and commuted the sentences of a dozen members of far-right groups the Proud Boys and the Oath Keepers. Trump defended these pardons, saying "these people have been destroyed".

Bis, the White House spokesperson, said on Monday that what Biden and his administration "did to this country should never be forgotten".

She asserted they "created the worst border crisis in history, were soft-on-crime, produced the worst inflation crisis in 40 years, and championed America-Last policies".

What happened on 6 January at the Capitol riot?

The excerpt of Biden's memoir also detailed a long meeting between himself and Trump following the latter's 2024 election victory.

Biden wrote that he was shocked when Trump purportedly said: "if it weren't for politics, I believe we'd be good friends".

The former president said the statement left him "too stunned to respond".

"He said my performance on job creation had been 'extraordinary,'" Biden wrote. "He added that he'd been relieved he didn't have to run against me. I didn't really understand why he was buttering me up, so I cut off his compliments to move on to the business at hand."

Biden's memoir comes on the back of Democrats' success in midterm elections last week.

He was not seen much on the campaign trail as he has continued treatment for prostate cancer and has said he is limiting a promotional tour for his book because of this treatment.

"Some days are better than others," Biden said in a social media post on Sunday about his cancer experience. "It hasn't stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down."

articles.title: Feud between former Trump officials exposes divisions over MAHA movement after midterm losses
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — A public spat between former Trump administration officials over alleged corruption in public health policymaking is the latest front in Re...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A public spat between former Trump administration officials over alleged corruption in public health policymaking is the latest front in Republicans' postelection recriminations, a battle that has exposed fault lines within the White House and could reshape political alliances involving the influential Make America Healthy Again movement.

The blowup began when Calley Means , a former top adviser to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and a chief advocate for the MAHA movement , appeared on Joe Rogan's podcast Friday and accused Susie Wiles, James Blair and others of catering to foreign and domestic lobbyists at the expense of Americans' health.

Wiles, who was recently replaced as White House chief of staff, and Blair, a top political adviser, have denied the allegations.

Means' remarks came days after voters cast ballots in midterm elections where government corruption was among the top issues for voters who ousted Republicans and handed Democrats control of Congress.

The issue overlaps with concerns from MAHA activists, who have been focused on combating what they see as systemic and harmful corporate influence over policymaking. MAHA became an important part of Trump's coalition after Kennedy endorsed him during the last presidential campaign, and fractures could create political headaches or new avenues for congressional investigations in the coming years.

Zen Honeycutt, a former Kennedy campaign staffer and founder of the group Moms Across America, said Means is "amplifying the frustrations that a lot of MAHA folks have had the past few months and validating them." She's "excited for a new beginning" now that Trump has replaced Wiles with Stephen Miller, whom she views as more aligned with the movement.

But Honeycutt hasn't ruled out working with Democrats, such as New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, whom she met with in July to discuss shared environmental priorities, including the pesticide glyphosate and artificial intelligence data centers.

"The MAHA movement does not belong to any party or politician," Honeycutt said.

Means alleges outside interests influenced policymaking

On Rogan's show, Means recounted a conversation he had with Wiles about her declining to support certain MAHA initiatives because she needed donations from the sugar industry. "Calley, we can't do this. I need sugar money," he recalled Wiles saying to him. "I need the money from the sugar people to win the midterms."

"There is a very concentrated group in the Trump administration that are antagonistic to what people voted for," Means said. Rogan's show was released Friday, shortly before Trump announced Wiles would step down as White House chief of staff.

Means was hired as a White House adviser early in the second Trump administration. He used his perch at the Health and Human Services Department to attack the nation's leading physician groups, federal agencies and government scientists , claiming they only protect their own interests . Means left the Trump administration in October, without stating a reason for his exit.

"She has taken a stranglehold on any policy decision" impacting the MAHA movement, alongside her former lobbying firm Ballard Partners, Means said about Wiles.

Referring to Blair in the Rogan interview, Means said he has "explicitly catered to special interests against the will of the voters." He said he believed much of what he was alleging "happened without Trump's full knowledge."

Blair, who previously served as a White House deputy chief of staff before taking an outside role in Trump's political operation, responded on social media that he was contemplating suing Means over his statements.

In text messages between Means and Blair, viewed by The Associated Press, Blair told Means "if you get near slandering or defaming me I will sue you," and "if you are gonna try to knife me, I'm happy to return the favor."

The White House denied Means' accusations.

"The Trump Administration has never allowed and will never allow outside groups to influence policy decisions," White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said.

Brian Ballard, founder of Ballard Partners, denied communicating with top White House officials on glyphosate and other issues in a statement posted on social media.

The extraordinary public fight, which was continuing on social media Monday, comes after MAHA had grown disenchanted over some of the administration's moves.

In recent months, many grassroots MAHA activists who had initially hoped to collaborate with Trump's Environmental Protection Agency had soured on the agency and the administration, viewing them as infiltrated by lobbyist interests.

They pointed to various insiders in the agricultural and chemical industries who'd secured high-level positions in the EPA and blamed them for the administration's failure to pass meaningful reforms to address microplastics in drinking water or pesticides on farms.

EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin promised last December to unveil a formal agenda of MAHA policies he would act on. But by the summer, the so-called MAHA agenda had never surfaced, and an EPA spokesperson told the AP that MAHA is an ongoing effort, rather than a single report.

That apparent reversal prompted several activists to say they planned to vote on issues over party in November's elections.

"People are done with the profits of corporations being prioritized over public health," Alexandra Muñoz, a molecular toxicologist who collaborates with MAHA activists on certain issues, told the AP in July. "And I think that will have an important role in the midterms."

The simmering MAHA frustration, coupled with Means' allegations, could put MAHA support in play for Democrats, something Means himself suggested over the weekend.

"There's a lot of complicated issues that I'm sure Democrats are going to want to address. But when it comes to these issues on MAHA, I think there is huge opportunity in the next year to get some big things done," he told CBS' "Face the Nation."

But doing so poses its own complications.

Democrats who will take over both chambers of Congress next year could use Means' statements as a vehicle to begin investigations into White House officials. Some Democrats have long sought to investigate Kennedy over his upending of vaccine policy and his vast cuts to science research, among other decisions. Pushing hard against Kennedy, however, could complicate efforts to build closer ties with MAHA supporters, many of whom still view the health secretary positively.

Means' interviews included a profuse defense of Kennedy, who some have speculated could attempt another run for president in 2028. Means called Kennedy a "hero" on the podcast interview.

articles.title: SCOTUS allows Trump admin to temporarily resume border construction in Texas' Big Bend
articles.summary: The Supreme Court lifted a federal injunction blocking Trump border wall construction in the Big Bend Sector, but environmental groups' lawsuit continues.
articles.body: The U. S. Supreme Court on Monday cleared the way for the Trump administration to resume border wall construction in West Texas, granting an emergency request from the federal government to lift a lower court's hold on the project. The justices' ruling stays a preliminary injunction issued last month by a federal district judge in El Paso, who had temporarily halted border wall construction in the region designated by U. S. Customs and Border Protection as the Big Bend Sector while litigation proceeds. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson indicated she would have denied the stay request but did not file a written dissent. LIBERAL JUSTICE HAMMERS SUPREME COURT FOR FAST-TRACKING EMERGENCY DOCKET CASES The lawsuit against the project was brought by a coalition of environmental groups and local residents, who claim the Department of Homeland Security violated constitutional provisions by proceeding without congressional authorization and bypassing environmental regulations. Spanning more than 500 miles, the Big Bend Sector covers roughly a quarter of the U. S.–Mexico border, though it accounted for just 1. 3% of all border apprehensions in 2025, Reuters reported. MULLIN TELLS CONGRESS PRIMARY BORDER WALL WILL BE DONE BY JUNE 2027, SECONDARY WALL BY SUMMER 2028 Administration officials have argued the wall is vital to stopping cartel operations active south of the border and curbing the smuggling of large quantities of illicit drugs into the U.S. Most of the proposed construction in the Big Bend Sector will take place on privately owned land, according to administration officials. Big Bend National Park is slated for a 17-mile barrier, though officials noted it will not feature the 30-foot steel pedestrian fencing planned in other areas along the southern border. articles.title: Trump casts doubt on election results after saying he was ‘absolutely willing’ to accept them
articles.summary: “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest,” the president asked on social media, without offering evidence of election interference.
articles.body: Days after saying he was “absolutely willing” to accept the massive Republican losses in the midterm elections, President Donald Trump suggested Monday on social media that the Democratic victories weren’t “honest.” “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong??? Some early voting ‘dumps’ were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to vote,” he wrote on Truth Social, implying there was something nefarious about elections carried out under different processes in different states. “It’s all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!” the post concluded, without elaborating. Election officials nationwide have reported that voting this year was largely routine. Trump, speaking to reporters later in the day, was asked whether he thought the midterms had been rigged. “Well, I think the numbers were terrible in terms of those early votes. You look at all those early votes,” he said, before he pivoted to talking about the still-undecided Senate race in Alaska. A White House official, asked earlier in the day about the president’s post, noted that Trump had told reporters ahead of last week’s elections that he would respect the results “if they’re honest elections.” In the lead-up to the election, the Justice Department sent a number of legal letters raising the specter of noncitizen voting and fraud in a number of Democratic-led states, which a judge found was an attempt to intimidate election officials. Trump has a history of denying election results. His previous false claims include that the 2016 Iowa caucuses were rigged against him when he lost to Sen. Ted Cruz, that he won the national popular vote in 2016 despite losing it by almost 3 million votes, and that he won the 2020 election despite losing it by 7 million votes. Yet, by the time election night arrived last week and the scale of Democrats’ victory became clear, Trump suggested he would accept the midterm results — while noting that he was not on the ballot. “I’m absolutely willing to accept those results,” Trump told The New York Times in an interview Tuesday night. “I’m going to become a Political Pundit, both good and bad, on the reasons these Candidates won and lost!” he wrote that night on Truth Social. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” he wrote in another. In an interview with “60 Minutes” that aired Sunday, Trump ran through a number of reasons why Republicans lost, including that his deportation policies “might be too tough” and that voters “didn’t like the war. They didn’t like that gasoline was up.” “In some cases, they didn’t like the candidates, and that’s their prerogative,” Trump said in the interview, which was taped Friday. “I was not on the ballot, but I campaigned hard for some people, and I think if I was on the ballot, it would have been a much different situation, because you saw the level of popularity and love,” he said. His stance seemed to start to shift Saturday, after he replaced longtime chief of staff Susie Wiles with MAGA favorite Stephen Miller. That was the day Trump on Truth Social reposted an X user who questioned how so many states could have had their votes swing by 15% in the midterm elections. “A pattern this even demands answers at the ballot level: paper ballot hand counts, poll-book check-ins against votes counted, and voter files showing who actually turned out,” the post said. Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar, a Democrat, told NBC News that Trump’s claims about the election are “completely false.” “The systems worked,” and “the election was a massive rebuke of his leadership,” Aguilar said in a phone interview. “He’s upset because he lost and people are holding him accountable,” he added. Claims about a rigged election were sparse as polls opened and results came in. Most focused on casting a conspiratorial shadow on real mishaps caused by bad weather in Arizona and malfunctioning machines in Westchester County, New York. In the latter case, election officials followed established contingency plans to use backup machines and said all votes cast would be counted. The incidents got little pickup from influential accounts, and Trump paid them little mind on his own social media channels. Researchers at the University of Washington who were tracking false narratives on election night told reporters their early analysis shows the spread of such rumors was much smaller at the onset of the night than during elections past. Immediately following election night, those rumors died down. “What’s missing for election denialism this cycle? Widespread shared grievance,” Kate Starbird, a professor at the university, wrote in a series of social media posts Sunday analyzing the rigged election rumors, noting that the false narrative seems to have drifted back to the fringes even as the president puts renewed effort into boosting them. In an interview Monday, Starbird said that Trump’s post caused an immediate spike in election denialism chatter on X. But she said Trump is still missing some of the ingredients he would need in order to mobilize his supporters into real-world action, as he did after the 2020 presidential election. “It’s a trial balloon. He’s going to see if his audience likes it,” she told NBC News. “He can walk away from it or he can double down,” she said. “If it’s just the hardcore conspiracy theorists reposting him, he may lose energy if he can’t push it beyond that group.” One person who quickly raised questions online about the integrity of the election after Democrats made larger-than-anticipated gains in the House, the Senate and various state legislatures was MyPillow founder Mike Lindell, a Trump ally who’s made numerous debunked claims about the 2020 election. Lindell was hit with a $2 million defamation judgment related to those claims last year. While Lindell had previously made unfounded allegations about foreign interference, the allegations this time around are focused on “matching algorithmic patterns.” Trump now appears to be focused on the numbers, as well, but it’s unclear which polls he was referring to when he wrote, “How could the Polls be so wrong???” The polls this election cycle underestimated the size of Democrats’ winning margin, although they “captured the direction of this year’s election,” the Pew Research Center said in a preliminary analysis posted Friday. Trump had previously said the “actual” polls showed Republicans winning and dismissed polling that showed Democrats would take control of the House and might take control of the Senate as “fake.” Democrats wound up overperforming in even those polls. “The Radical Left Democrats are going CRAZY with Fake Polls,” he wrote on Truth Social in August. “They’re putting them out at levels never seen before. They’re called, ‘Demoralization Operations,’ where they try to demoralize Republicans so that they don’t go out and vote — But the actual Polls are tremendous, and the Spirit in our Country has never been higher. We’re winning against EVERYONE,” he wrote. Aguilar said that “election officials cannot and do not pay attention to” opinion polls. “We follow the law,” he said.
